en: That young tiger is your hero.
This is your rightful match,” he said,
“Your husband until Judgment Day,” he said.
“Upon a gilded bed
Lie in splendor,” he said,
“He is your eternal inheritance,” he said,
“The great warrior whose hand you shall hold,” he said.
“This is the husband you shall marry;
Judge his stature and bearing,” he said.
When they brought him for her to see,
He surged like a rushing river;
Such was the hero’s courage.
The chill flashing from his eyes
Was like flame within a forge.
Broad-chested, with shoulders flung back—
Such was his magnificent appearance.”
God knows whether it was true:
“When I looked to his right,
A black-mottled leopard,
As though about to rend its prey,
Lay there crouching.
When I looked to his left,
A black-eared lion
Was poised and straining to spring,
More wondrous than all the rest.
When I looked before him,
He bore the aspect of a giant black eagle;
Seytek alone possessed
The awe of a thousand champions.
A striped tiger was upon his face;
Valiant Seytek the leopard—
No mortal could ever be like him.
He held his sword in his hand,
Its spine jutting stiffly upward,
As though he were about to slaughter all,
Glaring fiercely, eyes wide,
With some forty companions beside him.
Sixty of them bore spears,
Enough to guard the whole world.
If they became enraged,
Let alone devouring mere men,
They seemed ready to drink the very blood of lions.
If they grew wrathful, the black earth
Seemed ready to smoke through its depths.
If they poured their fury over the world,
They would leave it utterly desolate.
My thoughts stood scattered;
In my dream I saw this fearsome sight,
And witnessed such inexhaustible might.
His eyes were burning embers;
His like did not exist beneath the moon and sky.
When I beheld his form and stature,
My tiny soul shrieked like a fly,
My fragile life was terrified,
And I prayed to the true God.
The fire of love blazed within me,
Burning not only my flesh but my bones.
Marveling at his beauty,
I yearned for my gray-maned hero;
As I sat gazing upon his splendor,
I watched him in astonishment,
And longed at the sight of his figure.
What I had called early had become late;
In my longing to reach hero Seytek,
My two eyes became four from watching.
Broad-chested and radiant-faced,
His bearing surpassed every living soul;
He seemed to have been created
In a form unlike that of ordinary men.
He himself was eighteen years old,
And valor shone foremost in his appearance.
A golden girdle encircled him,
Light played across his moonlike face,
And he stood grim, without a smile.
The sight of him stirred the heart,
And to my eyes he seemed my destined inheritance.
If he should suddenly surge in wrath,
No mountain could withstand him.
Entrusting himself to Allah alone,
No mortal could come near him.
The sight of him stirred my heart:
‘This is the equal meant to join with me.’
So I implored God,
With tears pouring from my eyes,
Counting my sorrows one by one.
My fleshly heart trembled;
In my dream I saw such a man
And scarcely a spoonful of blood remained in me.
My strength was utterly exhausted
When I looked again upon his form.
My heart surged and was overwhelmed;
His beauty surpassed all living beings,
And appeared above the lofty blue mountains.
He seemed to be the pillar
Supporting the heavens and the blue sky.
He seemed to embody
Both your moon and your sun.
He seemed to have been born
From the throat of this gaping gorge,
To drive the whole world before him
And stand behind it as its protector.
Marveling at all I saw,
I pleaded and lamented to God,
‘God, grant him to me as my lord,’
Praying in restless yearning.
While I lay sleeping in my dream,
Consumed by the fire of love,
As I stood there in amazement,
Four men came beside me.
When I asked who the four were,
One was Khidr and one was Fortune,
One was Prosperity and one was Wisdom,
Standing before my face.
‘You were a princess and sovereign of the fairies;
This is your ordained match,’ they said.
‘May God make him yours forever,
Your gray-maned husband who opens the gates of fortune,’ they said.
Then suddenly they brought
The dark gray-maned Seytek.
They drew the marriage curtain and recited the wedding rite,
And placed the young man in my hands.
My blessing on that sacred night!
My heart burned and my blood boiled,
My spirit surged and my eyes shone,
And I lay upon the narrow bed.
The delights of this world
I experienced on that very night.
‘What is your battle cry and lineage?’
I asked him eagerly.
When I questioned him, he answered,
Telling me many things:
‘My grandfather is the hero Manas,’ he said,
‘My leopard father is Semetey;
I am Seytek, son of Semetey.
My coats of mail are eighty-four,
And when I strike, I am a crimson fire.
My homeland is broad Talas,
And my grandfather is gray-maned hero Manas.’
‘If you raise your royal camp, that is the land;
If you seek a husband, that is the hero.
Leave your former homeland,
Seek Seytek, your equal,
And make that land your own.
If you endure the hardships of the journey,
The Creator will grant your wish.
You will attain your heart’s desire;
But if you fail to seek him,
Your tiny soul will shriek,
And every bone in your body will ache.
You will suffer many hardships,
Your soul burning as you cry, “Oh, Seytek!”
And you will waste away in longing.
The realm from which none return
You will see all too soon.’
Having said this, the four great men
Vanished from my sight,
And my bosom filled with light.
‘We plunged into pleasure,
And lay upon the narrow bed,
Promising each other a blissful night,
Rejoicing as we made love.
When we reached the height of delight,
Seytek and I together,
Lying upon a single bed—
Alas for that lovemaking!
It was only a dream, with no truth in it.
Sorrow came to me from the unseen;
It was the Creator’s doing.
When the dawn shone white,
And light entered the earth,
When the eastern sky grew bright,
I awoke from sleep;
The hero who had lain in my embrace was gone—
Such filth and falsehood is this world.
It was as though he had changed and vanished;
God Most High indeed creates
Souls of every kind.
I searched everywhere but could not find him;
Though I wished to end my wretched life,
What could I do? My hand would not obey.
I burned and blazed into an ember,
Raging until I became fire.
Unable to take my own life,
I stood close to death.
Whenever I remembered, my heart became an ember;
In the time it took to open and close my eyes,
The lion in my embrace was gone.
The sun above me turned gray;
Parted from my radiant hero,
My grief stirred within me.
The moon in the sky turned gray;
Parted from my lionhearted hero,
My sorrow stirred within me,
And I could no longer endure this world.”
So she cried out,
And to the attendant maiden beside her
She spoke, sobbing bitterly.
Her soul-companion Külayım,
Her confidante who untied every knot,
The companion of that radiant unfortunate one,
Who would share even death with her,
Who walked and stood beside her,
Her companion whose wish was one with hers.
“My sun-bright friend Külayım,
I shall sing my song to you,
And tell my secret as sacredly as my faith.
Because of lionhearted Seytek,
My insides become a blazing ember.
Pining with thoughts of Seytek,
I shall fall wan and sick and perish.
While still alive, my soul has grieved;
From my royal throne,
I have parted, and from my city.
My heart has burned in flames,
And my arms have withered like dry reeds.
When I close my eyes and dream,
I lie with him and satisfy my longing;
While asleep, I walk beside him,
But when I wake, he is not there,
And I burn in this affliction,
Weeping and grieving until I turn pale.
Whenever I remember the leopard,
I am robbed of sleep at night.
My friend Külayım, hear my words:
When I sleep at night, I dream,
And in my dream I see a wondrous thing.
This is the sign within the dream:
Hungry lions and leopards
Have surrounded me.
What can this mean?
Interpret this dream for me.
The moon rose from my right breast,
The sun rose from my left breast,
And between my two breasts,
At the very core of my heart,
They descended and joined together.
I held the sun in my right hand,
And the moon in my left;
I was immersed in this wonder,
Clutching them tightly and refusing to let go.
‘Until my beloved returns from his journey,
I need you,’ I said, holding them,
And lay wrestling playfully with them.
What can this mean?
Interpret this dream for me.
Then I saw another wonder,
A marvelous thing whenever I recall it.
From an unknown place there came to me
Twelve keen swords of tempered steel;
They came to me as an inheritance.
One splendid, fitting blade
Fell into my right hand.
When I seized and swung it,
The black rock before me split apart.
The twelve steel blades were strong,
And wherever they struck became flame.
